summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: Virginia - Va. Code Title 63.2, Chapter 15 (Child Abuse and Neglect – includes § 63.2-1509 reporting)
Virginia - Va. Code § 16.1-241(A) et seq. (Juvenile & Domestic Relations jurisdiction for abuse/neglect)

regulations_applicable.title: 22VAC40-705 - Child Protective Services (Virginia Administrative Code, Title 22, Agency 40)
22VAC40-201 - Permanency Services: Prevention, Foster Care, Adoption and Independent Living

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Weaver v. Roanoke Department of Human Resources
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court of Virginia reversed the termination of both parents' residual parental rights because the record contained no evidence that social agencies made the 'reasonable and appropriate efforts' that Code § 16.1-283(C)(2) requires before rights may be severed, and directed that termination statutes be read to preserve the parent-child relationship where possible.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion states Virginia's governing preference for preserving the parent-child relationship, the legal anchor for reunification as the default outcome.
key_cases.quote: Statutes terminating the legal relationship between parent and child should be interpreted consistently with the governmental objective of preserving, when possible, the parent-child relationship.

key_cases.case_name: Harris v. Lynchburg Division of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court of Virginia affirmed termination as to the mother but reversed as to the father, holding that undisputed evidence that a parent was never offered or provided services overcomes the statutory prima facie case and puts the agency to full proof of the § 16.1-283(C)(2) factors.
key_cases.relevance: The Court ordered the father given the offer and an opportunity to show what progress he could make, i.e., a genuine chance at reunification.
key_cases.quote: where, as here, there is undisputed evidence that a parent has not been offered or provided services, the prima facie case is overcome

key_cases.case_name: C.S. v. Virginia Beach Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals of Virginia reversed, vacated and remanded a termination under Code § 16.1-283(C)(2), holding that the evidence fell short of clear and convincing proof that the mother had failed to remedy substantially the conditions leading to foster care placement.
key_cases.relevance: The Court found the mother had in fact remedied the conditions, restoring the reunification path the trial court had cut off.
key_cases.quote: the evidence falls short of the standard of clear and convincing proof that mother did not remedy substantially the conditions which led to the child's foster care placement

key_cases.case_name: Adam Yafi v. Stafford Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals of Virginia affirmed termination under Code § 16.1-283(E), holding that where a parent is convicted of felony child abuse causing serious bodily injury to a sibling or subjects a child to aggravated circumstances, the Department need not prove it offered reasonable and appropriate rehabilitative services.
key_cases.relevance: It identifies the aggravated-circumstances situations in which Virginia law removes reunification and reasonable efforts from the case entirely.
key_cases.quote: the termination of Yafi’s residual parental rights under Code § 16.1-283(E)(iii) and 16.1-283(E)(iv) did not require a predicate showing that DSS provided any services to Yafi

key_cases.case_name: Rocka v. Roanoke County Department of Public Welfare
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court of Virginia reversed an order granting a welfare board permanent custody with the right to place for adoption, holding that in a contest between a parent and a non-parent the rule of comparative best interests does not apply and the board must prove parental unfitness by clear and convincing evidence, and directing an interlocutory award of custody to the mother so she could demonstrate her present fitness.
key_cases.relevance: The Court ordered an interlocutory award of custody to the mother for at least six months so she could demonstrate her capacity, the clearest early Virginia statement that reunification is the default when the agency's proof falls short.
key_cases.quote: We believe that the evidence of parental unfitness in this record is less than clear and convincing and, thus, insufficient to divest a parent of custody of its child.

key_cases.case_name: Berrien v. Greene County Department of Public Welfare
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court of Virginia reversed an order terminating a mother's parental rights and entered final judgment restoring custody to her, holding that even though credible evidence supported the trial court's best-interests finding, the Department bore and failed to carry the burden of proving parental unfitness before rights could be permanently terminated.
key_cases.relevance: Rather than remand, the Court ordered custody of the child restored to her natural mother, the strongest Virginia authority that reunification follows when the agency fails to prove unfitness.
key_cases.quote: the burden was on the Department to prove Berrien's unfitness before the trial court could take the ultimate, drastic, and irrevocable step of permanently terminating her parental rights

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (Fostering Futures; voluntary, conditions apply; Va. Code § 63.2-917)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
